s: Laws for the burnt offering, given wholly to God.
Laws for the grain offering.
Laws for the peace offering, shared in fellowship.
Offerings for sins committed in ignorance by priests, leaders and people.
Offerings for particular sins and for guilt.
More rules on guilt offerings and on the priests' part in the sacrifices.
Rules for the guilt and peace offerings and what the priests may eat.
Moses consecrates Aaron and his sons as priests.
Aaron offers the first sacrifices, and fire from the Lord consumes them.
Nadab and Abihu offer unholy fire and are struck dead. Rules for the priests' conduct.
Which animals are clean to eat and which are unclean.
Purification of a mother after childbirth.
Rules for recognizing leprosy and other skin diseases.
How a healed leper is cleansed, and how to treat infected houses.
Rules of cleanness concerning bodily discharges.
The Day of Atonement: the high priest enters the Holy of Holies, and a scapegoat carries the people's sins into the desert.
Sacrifice belongs only at the tabernacle. Blood must not be eaten, for life is in the blood.
Forbidden marriages and sexual practices, which defiled the nations before them.
Be holy, for I am holy. Laws on daily life, including love your neighbour as yourself.
Penalties for idolatry, child sacrifice and grave sexual sins.
Rules of holiness for the priests.
Rules about who may eat the holy offerings and which animals may be offered.
The feasts of the year: sabbath, Passover, Pentecost, Trumpets, the Day of Atonement and Tabernacles.
The lamp and the holy bread. A man who blasphemes the Name is stoned.
The sabbath year and the jubilee every fiftieth year, when land returns to its family and slaves go free.
Blessings for obedience and curses for disobedience. God will remember his covenant even in exile.
Rules for vows and dedicated gifts, and the tithe.

16: Once a year the high priest enters the Holy of Holies with blood to make atonement for the people. The letter to the Hebrews shows Christ doing this once for all.
